case.background: A fixed amount of air is trapped above mercury in a sealed J-tube. Add mercury pressure while holding the thermal condition fixed, then infer how pressure and air volume are related.
initial_observations: Adding mercury compresses the trapped air reversibly.
The bath prevents deliberate temperature changes during a run.

controls.description: Condition of the surrounding bath during compression.
controls.name: thermal_condition

instruments.description: A sealed J-tube with trapped air, mercury, and pressure and volume scales.
instruments.name: sealed_j_tube

notes: The trapped amount of air and its temperature remain fixed.
Any non-empty subset of the two listed readouts may be requested.

FinalSubmission.model must equal 'expression'. FinalSubmission.parameters must equal {'outputs': {READOUT: EXPR, ...}} with exactly these readouts: air_volume_ml, absolute_pressure_kpa. experiment.intent: Measure equilibrium air volume and absolute pressure at several added mercury pressures under constant room temperature to distinguish inverse P-V behavior from linear volume-pressure decrease.

hypotheses.statement: At fixed temperature and amount of air, absolute pressure and volume are inversely related so that P*V is constant: P = P0 + x and V = C/(P0 + x), where x is added pressure kPa.
At fixed temperature, trapped air volume decreases approximately linearly with added mercury pressure over the tested range: V = V0 - s*x, while absolute pressure equals ambient plus added pressure.
